cards.title: Arrays hold lists
cards.body: An array keeps values in order inside square brackets. `nums[0]` is the first item and `nums.length` is how many there are.

cards.title: Reading a line of numbers
cards.body: `split(" ")` cuts text at spaces into an array of pieces, and `.map(Number)` turns each piece into a number.

cards.title: for...of
cards.body: `for (const x of nums)` visits each item of an array in order.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print the last item, 15, but prints `undefined`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Indexes start at 0, so the last one is `nums.length - 1`: `nums[nums.length - 1]`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: `a.length` is 3, so `a[2]` is the last item, 7. Indexes start at 0.

exercise.prompt: Read whole numbers on one line, separated by spaces, and print their total.
exercise.starterCode:
const nums = prompt().split(" ").map(Number);
// print the total of nums
